'''Lingle:''' {{legend0|#ffb2b2|40–50%}} {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Ben Cayetano]] | after_election = [[Ben Cayetano]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsHI}} The '''1998 Hawaii gubernatorial election''' was held on November 3, 1998. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Ben Cayetano]] was re-elected to a second term in office over [[Mayor of Maui County|Maui County mayor]] [[Linda Lingle]]. Cayetano won narrowly despite Lingle holding a sizable advantage in public opinion polling.{{Cite web|last=Silver|first=Nate|date=2014-11-06|title=Why Polls Missed A Shocker In Virginia's Senate Race|url=https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/mark-warner-why-polls-missed-a-shocker-in-virginias-senate-race/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141107022928/http://fivethirtyeight.com/features/mark-warner-why-polls-missed-a-shocker-in-virginias-senate-race/|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 7, 2014|access-date=2020-09-26|website=FiveThirtyEight|language=en-US}} This is the second election, along with [[1966 Hawaii gubernatorial election|1966]], in which a Democratic candidate won without sweeping every county in the state.
